10.1002_adma.75260: Employing functional lithium salts in electrolytes is an effective strategy to suppress anode instabilities and sluggish charge‐transfer kinetics in lithium batteries. However, high solubility requirements intrinsically exclude a broad class of promising, high‐lattice‐energy inorganic salts for carbonate electrolytes. Here, we establish an immobilized functional platform (IFP) by deploying insoluble lithium salts with strong Lewis‐acidic Li + sites directly onto an aramid‐scaffolded separator. This design bypasses conventional dissolution–diffusion limitations, yielding a thin, ionically conductive, LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) driven by regulated interfacial Li + solvation and enhanced anion‐derived decomposition. Systematic screening and 6 Li/ 7 Li isotope tracing identify Li 2 SO 4 (LS) as the optimal IFP candidate (IFP‐LS) owing to its moderate Lewis acidity, superior solvent affinity, and industrial viability. Remarkably, LS provides a finite sacrificial lithium contribution during continuous SEI evolution, mitigating irreversible lithium consumption. Consequently, IFP‐LS separators quadruple the lifespan of Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 cells at 0.7 C compared to bare separators, and deliver 88.4% capacity retention over 2400 cycles in Li||LiFePO 4 cells at 5 C. Scalability is further validated through 100 m roll‐to‐roll manufacturing across diverse Ah‐level formats, adding only 0.163 USD m −2 . This work overcomes the lithium salt solubility barrier and unlocks a vast library of potent materials for next‐generation high‐energy‐density batteries.
10.1002_anie.1984422: In situ polymerized quasi‐solid‐state electrolytes (QSEs) are promising for lithium metal batteries (LMBs) yet face challenges regarding high‐voltage stability and kinetics. Herein, a novel ether‐ester hybrid QSE is achieved through the in situ copolymerization of 2,2,2‐trifluoroethyl acrylate (TFEA) and 2‐isocyanatoethyl methacrylate (IEM) within a tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether (G4)/fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) solvent system. This design leverages synergistic interactions between the functionalized polymer matrix (─CF 3 and ─N═C═O) and liquid components. The incorporation of FEC and the regulatory effect of the polymer backbone tailor the Li + solvation structure toward an anion‐rich configuration, which gives rise to a robust, antioxidative, and inorganic‐rich interphase. Furthermore, hydrogen bonding interactions effectively immobilize PF 6 − anions and free G4 molecules, thereby elevating the Li + transference number and enabling the electrochemical stability window over 4.8 V (vs. Li + /Li). The QSE exhibited a high room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.2 × 10 −3 S cm −1 . Consequently, 4.2 V Li|| LiFePO 4 (LFP) cells demonstrate 93% capacity retention over 1,000 cycles, while 4.5 V Li||NCM811 (NCM811) cells retain 80% over 300 cycles. A specific energy of 302.64 Wh kg −1 is attained in a 2 Ah Li||NCM811 pouch‐type cell. These findings highlight tailored molecular design and controlled interactions as a viable route for advancing high‐energy‐density quasi‐solid‐state batteries.
10.1002_anie.9300778: The long‐standing trade‐off between ion selectivity and ionic conductivity in membrane materials stems from the difficulty in rapidly transporting ions through chemically homogeneous channels while simultaneously excluding large ions. Here, we report a solvation‐gradient membrane prepared via reaction‐diffusion‐coupled interfacial polymerization between piperazine and 1,3,5‐tris(bromomethyl)benzene. The resulting membrane comprised a dense outer selective layer approximately 35 nm thick (with a transport pore size of approximately 6 Å) and an NH‐rich inner layer approximately 400 nm thick. The outer layer imposes a high entry/desolvation barrier on large ions, thereby inhibiting their transport, whereas the NH‐rich region supports rapid OH − transport through re‐solvation and hydrogen‐bond reorganization. This depth‐dependent architecture spatially separates ferricyanide rejection from hydroxide conduction. Depth‐resolved spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations supported a depth‐dependent solvation environment and revealed stronger water/OH − interactions in the NH‐rich region. Optimization of poly(tertiary amine) (PTA) membranes achieved low Fe(CN) 6 3− permeability (8.07 × 10 −7 cm 2 h −1 ) and OH − conductivity (41.08 mS cm −1 ), enabling an alkaline zinc‐iron flow battery to achieve an energy efficiency of 89.94% at 80 mA cm −2 and stable cycling for over 800 h. This study suggests depth‐dependent solvation regulation as a useful design principle for alleviating the selectivity‐conductivity trade‐off in electrochemical membranes.
10.1016_j.electacta.2026.149622: This work reports the development of a novel dual electrochemical reactor based on membrane–electrode assemblies (MEAs) for the simultaneous, in situ production of ozone (O 3 ) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ). In this system, water oxidation takes place at the anode–membrane interface and the generated protons are transported through a proton-exchange membrane (Nafion) to the cathode, allowing the anolyte to be deionized water. This configuration avoids the use of conductive anodic electrolytes, which is essential to prevent the formation of oxoanions and other oxidizing species that scavenge ozone and reduce process efficiency, particularly when diamond-based anodes are employed. To address the difficulty of integrating gas diffusion electrodes (GDEs) into MEAs, an alternative cathodic configuration is proposed, in which the GDE is extended using an electrically conductive carbon felt. This design ensures continuous oxygen supply and enlarges the effective cathodic surface area, reducing the local current density and enabling hydrogen peroxide formation under the same applied current required for ozone generation at the anode. Because the anolyte is deionized water, the catholyte composition controls the overall cell resistance, operating voltage, and oxidant selectivity. Low ionic strength catholytes such as NaHCO 3 favor ozone production, reaching up to 15.7 mg h -1 with a current efficiency of 2.6 % at 1100 mA cm -2 , and a maximum energy efficiency of 0.969 g kWh -1 . In contrast, sulfate-based catholytes (Na 2 SO 4 ) allow operation at lower voltages and promote stable H 2 O 2 production (∼90 mg h -1 ), achieving a maximum energy efficiency of 17.7 g kWh -1 at 450 mA cm -2 . The results clearly demonstrate an antagonistic relationship between O 3 and H 2 O 2 formation as a function of current density. Finally, the electrogenerated oxidants proved effective for contaminant removal, benzene (BZN), highlighting the reactor’s potential for integrated advanced oxidation processes such as the peroxone system.
10.1021_acsami.6c13906: When compared to electrochromic devices (ECDs) that use other forms of ion transport, those that use small-sized protons as transport Ions have faster response rates. However, integrating high-concentration protons into robust all-inorganic solid-state ECDs is difficult. This work employed solid-state electrochemical techniques to replace sodium ions in phosphate glass with hydrogen ions, obtaining a proton conductor with a high proton concentration. Furthermore, under controlled heating conditions, a conductive reinforcing phase with low proton activation energy was induced to precipitate within the material, achieving room-temperature proton conduction. Based on this proton conductor as an electrolyte, a device with an "ITO/WO3/Proton conductor/NiO/ITO" structure was constructed by pulsed laser deposition, realizing the effective integration of protons in all-inorganic solid-state ECDs. The application restrictions of all-solid-state devices, which usually have slow response times, are overcome by this proton-transporting solid-state device's fast electrochromic effect (switching time close to 1s). This study presents a new strategy integrating fast switching for inorganic solid ECDs.
